To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the burrows of the macrofaunal species Scopimera infla~a. Uca spp. Callianassa australiensis. and Lingula anatina have different effects on infaunal community structure.

(1) the infaunal communities associated with burrows differ in abundance and composition to those in adjacent sediments; (2) the differences are mainly due to promotive interactions between infauna and burrowing animals; (3) the differences between burrows and sediments are not consistent in time; (4) the differences are not consistent between burrowing animals; and (5) in the case of burrows of the brachiopods L. anatjna,

the burrows of the 3 species of crustaceans and the brachiopd L. anatjna had a strong effect on the community structure of the infauna, and that this effect was mainly positive, i.e. the infaunal abund~nces were significantly higher in the burrows than in the surrounding sediments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the burrows of the 4 species of macrobenthos mentioned above.
the effects of the burrow environment of the infauna of tropical tidal flat sediments.
2 aspects of macrobenthos in the tropical region: 1) The effect of burrowing animals on infaunal community composition and 2) the effects of exclusion of burrowers on the community composition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the burrow walls are a habitat for meio- and microfauna, whereas the burrow chambers provide a habitat for macrofauna, and thus the burrow walls and the burrow chambers can be considered as 2 distinct habitats.
burrows have a positive effect on meiofauna, and a negative effect on macrofauna.
burrows are a habitat for many infauna.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the burrowers are important for the community structure of the infauna in the tropical tidal flats.

the burrows of crustaceans and brach~opods are important habitat for the associated meiobenthos and that the presence of the macrobenthic animals has a strong influence on the community of the adjacent sediment.
the effects of burrowers on the community are species specific and vary over time and space, but are generally promotive for infauna.
The main takeaway from our work is that
burrows of crustaceans and brachiopods are a significant component of the habitat for infauna on tropical tldal flats.
the presence of burrows in the sediment has a strong influence on the composition of the infaunal communities.
burrowing organisms can have a profound influence on the infauna, especially the meiofauna, and that this influence may vary with time and space.
